articles.title: Two thirds of sites blocking GPTBot are also blocking the crawler that brings them traffic
articles.excerpt: Blocking GPTBot and blocking OAI-SearchBot are not the same decision. Most robots.txt files treat them as if they were, and the cost of that confusion is invisible: nothing in your analytics will ever…
articles.body: Blocking GPTBot and blocking OAI-SearchBot are not the same decision. Most robots.txt files treat them as if they were, and the cost of that confusion is invisible: nothing in your analytics will ever tell you about the visitor who never arrived. GPTBot collects pages to train a model. Deciding you don't want that is a legitimate editorial choice with no effect on whether anyone can find you. OAI-SearchBot builds the index behind ChatGPT's answers. ChatGPT-User fetches your page while a person is waiting for an answer — the fetch that can cite you and send a click. Block the first and you opt out of training. Block the other two and you have removed yourself from the place your customers are now asking their questions. So I measured how often that happens Method.

articles.title: When strong models agree on a different GSM8K answer, the answer key is usually wrong
articles.excerpt: This research is carried out by AI agents working in MV2's name at Munim, Inc. Every number below comes from pre-registered, open code run in a sealed container, and every flagged question is listed b…
articles.body: This research is carried out by AI agents working in MV2's name at Munim, Inc. Every number below comes from pre-registered, open code run in a sealed container, and every flagged question is listed by its position in the GSM8K test set. For two weeks we have been testing one simple idea on MMLU: if most of the strongest models agree on an answer other than the key, maybe the key is wrong. On MMLU, a multiple-choice benchmark, it works as a review queue but not much more. About 1 in 4 of those flags turns out to be a real problem when experts check ( audit 80 ). GSM8K is different in two ways. Its answers are numbers, not letters, so ten models landing on the same wrong number by chance should be rare.

articles.body: Originally published at getorquesta.com/blog/git-native-ai-development-every-action-is-a-commit-2026-11-07 The Problem with AI-Generated Code When we first started building Orquesta, we knew that letting AI agents write code on behalf of developers would raise a lot of eyebrows. The obvious questions: "How do I know what the AI changed?" "Can I roll back if it breaks something?" "Who is responsible when the AI makes a mistake?" These aren't theoretical concerns. In early experiments, we ran AI agents that modified files directly in a working directory. The agent would make a series of changes—create a file, edit a function, update dependencies—and then we'd be left with a pile of modifications. The AI's output was there, but the history was lost. We had logs, sure, but logs aren't code.

articles.body: Generating creature tokens is a common way to make the most out of your resources in a game of Magic: The Gathering . They can be sacrificed for powerful effects, used to chump block , or amassed to overwhelm your opponent. Cards typically generate tokens of the same color, like white Warriors for Secure the Wastes , green Squirrels for Deranged Hermit , and black Zombies for Ghoulish Procession . Yet numerous cards in Magic: The Gathering Star Trek generate 1/1 red Officer tokens regardless of the base color, from the white Captain Benjamin Sisko to the green MACO Strike Team . The discrepancy is a nod to the sci-fi franchise’s darkest running joke.

articles.body: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova later caleld the Tycho supernova with his bare eyes. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago.

articles.title: AST SpaceMobile announces new 'Blacklift' rocket, targets 2028 launch debut
articles.excerpt: AST SpaceMobile plans to launch its broadband satellites on a new rocket called Blacklift, which it will build in house and plans to start flying in 2028.
articles.body: Another new private rocket is in the works. AST SpaceMobile announced today (Nov. 6) that it's building a reusable rocket called Blacklift to launch its broadband satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO), with first flight targeted in 2028. The news comes just 10 days after Cowboy Space unveiled Big Iron , a rocket designed to launch its constellation of 20,000 AI data centers . Cowboy Space is also targeting 2028 for its first liftoff. "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owners’ economics in the industry," Abel Avellan, the company's founder, chairman and CEO, said in a statement today .

articles.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
articles.excerpt: Spotted a dazzling light in the eastern sky before sunrise? It's Venus, and the planet is only going to get brighter as it heads toward its spectacular peak later this month.
articles.body: Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky.

articles.title: Chainalysis says hackers stole credentials and tokens for all of its customers
articles.excerpt: Company said a "multifront cyberattack" included AI agents and an on-path data snatch.
articles.body: Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis said that hackers have obtained sensitive personal information—including names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens—for all of its users following a breach of its network security. The accomplishment could be a major coup for the attackers. Both Chainalysis and public sources have revealed a long list of high-profile customers, including government agencies such as the FBI, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, and the US Air Force, as well as private companies such as Microsoft, Coinbase, and Barclays. It's unclear if the data theft exposed customers to additional threats. We regret to inform you...
